newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers still awaits Russian gem decision.
newsitem.headline: De Beers still awaits Russian gem decision.

text.p: De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd was still awaiting a Russian decision on a stalled diamond trade deal but hoped to be back on a contractual basis soon, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.

Russia's diamond-producing company Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS) said on April 3 that Russia would decide on April 15 whether to sign the trade deal with De Beers after a draft agreement was struck last year.
De Beers spokesman Tom Tweedy said the company was still awaiting the Russian decision with interest.
"We hope we will be back on a contractual basis soon. I think they will decide if they will sign it and probably decide when they will sign it," Tweedy said.
An ARS spokeswoman said on Tuesday that talks on the deal were continuing but a decision on whether to sign the deal may not be taken on Tuesday.
"All I know is that talks on the deal are continuing," she said. "We had expected agreement on the signing today, but it is still impossible to say exactly when the deal will go through."
Earlier this month ARS said Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais had said that the decision on whether to sign the deal or not would be taken on April 15.

Russia's Itar-Tass news agency, quoting a senior government source, also said on Tuesday that a presidential decree, needed before any agreement can come into effect, would be signed within the next 10 days.
De Beers, frustrated at Moscow's inability to communicate its position on a draft trade agreement submitted to the cabinet in October 1996, stopped buying stones from Russia at the end of last year.

ARS had said earlier that De Beers bought some ARS diamonds in February, but that the South African company was not able to export the diamonds because of Russian government delays in resolving export quota issues, which are part of a stalled deal.
